newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 16.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
- In one of the country's last big-city newspaper wars, neither The Denver Post nor The Rocky Mountain News is missing an opportunity to grab another reader.
- Delegates to the World Intellectual Property Organization of the United Nations are in Geneva to decide whether to ratify three controversial changes in international copyright treaties.
- American and Japanese negotiators worked out an agreement for providing greater foreign access to Japan's insurance market.
- Continental has ended merger talks with other airlines and has no immediate plans to restart them.
- Coca-Cola plans to challenge Mountain Dew with a new soft drink called Surge.

- In a move that shows how efforts by IBM and Motorola to establish a successful competitor to Intel 's Pentium computer chip are flagging, both companies are dropping support for the Windows NT operating system on computers built around their Power PC chip.
- William Bennett has unleashed a highly personal attack on MCA and its corporate overloard, Edward Bronfman Jr., for distributing music with lyrics Bennett says are violent and sexually degrading.
- CSC Index, the consulting firm that gave birth to the concept of re-engineering, is trying to re-engineer its own image, as the term has fallen out of favor.
